opennyai_summary.decision:
1. Exemption allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. The application stands disposed of.
CM APPL. 8026/2023 (delay 7 days)
3. This is an application preferred by the appellant seeking condonation of 7 days' delay in filing the appeal.
4. The application is, for the reasons stated therein, allowed.
Consequently, the delay of 7 days in filing the appeal stands condoned.
5. The application stands disposed of.
6. The present appeal, preferred by the insurer under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988,
seeks to assail the award dated 01.11.2022 passed by the learned Motor Accident Claim Tribunal,
insofar as the quantum of compensation is concerned.
7.
Upon the appellant taking steps, issue notice to respondent nos.1 to 3 through all permissible modes.
8. Taking into account that no recovery rights against the owner and driver of the offending vehicle have been granted by the learned Tribunal under the impugned award, no notice is required to be issued to respondent nos.4 & 5.
9.
10.This is an application filed by the appellant seeking stay of the impugned award.
11.Taking into account that the grievance of the appellant is confined to only non-deduction of amount towards income tax and regarding the amount of Rs. 1,32,000/- having been granted towards 'loss of consortium', the application is disposed of by directing the appellant to deposit,
within six weeks, a sum of Rs.60 lakh alongwith up-to-date interest thereon with the learned Tribunal with a further direction to the learned Tribunal to release the same in favour of the claimants as per the disbursal scheme contained in the impugned award.
12.Subject to the appellant depositing the amount in terms of this order, the operation of the impugned award will remain stayed during the pendency of the present appeal.
13.The application stands disposed of.
